plan: This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid. Bidding above my value risks paying more than the item is worth if I win but the price exceeds my value. Bidding below my value risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. Therefore, my optimal strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $3, ensuring I maximize expected profit regardless of others' bids.

This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy: if I bid exactly what the item is worth to me, I win whenever the price (second-highest bid) is below my value, ensuring positive profit, and I never overpay since I'd only pay what someone else bid, which would exceed my value only if I'd want to lose anyway. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item's worth to me; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Bidding exactly my value ensures I never overpay (I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, which will be less than my value) and never miss out on profitable wins. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth to me if the second-highest bid exceeds my value. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. My value is $11, so I will bid $11.
